forecasts.question: Will Netanyahu's coalition lose its Knesset majority or dissolve early before 2026-10-27?
forecasts.delta_reason: RESOLVED-NO (Judge override of Source A UPDATE proposal). The Knesset dissolved on July 17, 2026 via snap dissolution bill passed with 62 votes, initiated by Netanyahu's own coalition — not a crisis-driven majority loss and not a natural term completion (prior v48 note contained factual error; corrected per Al Jazeera Jul 17, Al-Monitor May 20, Reuters). Both YES-paths are permanently closed: (a) no roll-call majority-loss vote occurred before the dissolution, and (b) the election is scheduled ON October 27 (the horizon date), not before it, so the 'before 2026-10-27' resolution criterion is not satisfied. Netanyahu serves as caretaker PM and is the active Likud candidate.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a Knesset roll-call vote confirms coalition loss of majority (61 seats), OR if Netanyahu announces early dissolution and election date moves earlier than 2026-10-27. NO if coalition survives to mandatory election date with 61+ seats intact.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Knesset official record + Reuters/Haaretz/Times of Israel. Polling alone does not resolve.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: If coalition drops below 61 but Netanyahu remains caretaker PM until election: YES. If a single party departs but coalition retains 61+: NO. Reviewed weekly only (Sundays); no intra-week deltas.

forecasts.question: Will Iran publicly commit to resuming mediated ceasefire negotiations (a named Iranian official or MFA announces readiness for talks) before EOD 2026-09-06?
forecasts.delta_reason: RESOLVED-NO. The June 17 MOU collapsed by July 8, 2026, when both sides resumed hostilities and Iran initiated attacks on commercial vessels in the Strait of Hormuz. Between July 8 and September 6, no public Iranian commitment to resuming mediated ceasefire negotiations was confirmed by any wire service, government statement, or third-party mediator. The next confirmed diplomatic overture — Iran's seven-day Hormuz-for-sanctions proposal — was not formally submitted until UN General Assembly sidelines in late September 2026, weeks past the Sep 6 horizon. IRGC attacks on shipping through the Strait continued through the entire September 3-6 window.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if, before EOD 2026-09-06, a named Iranian official (FM Araghchi, Supreme National Security Council, or IRNA/Tasnim/Press TV quoting an official) issues a public statement committing to resuming or entering mediated ceasefire negotiations with the United States. A 'readiness for talks' declaration counts; mere written-message relay does NOT count.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: One TIER1 (Reuters/AP/AFP/Al Jazeera) citing the named Iranian official, OR Iranian state media (IRNA/Tasnim) carrying the official statement.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Conditional or preconditioned offers ('will talk if US stops strikes') = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO unless the US publicly accepts the condition; a mediator asserting Iran is 'open' without a named Iranian official statement = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.

forecasts.delta_reason: RESOLVED-NO. IMF PortWatch recorded approximately 25 vessels/day in late June, falling to ~10/day by July 13-19, ~1/day by September 27, and 4 vessels on October 4 (~5% of pre-crisis 85/day baseline). straitofhormuz.report showed ~3 ships/day 7-day rolling average on October 1 (~3% of 74/day norm). Divergence logged for calibration record; does not affect NO resolution.
